question: May traffic control devices or their supports carry advertising messages?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. The MUTCD flatly prohibits advertising on traffic control devices or their supports — they must display only messages related to traffic control. The same prohibition applies specifically to changeable message signs (CMS) and their supports and equipment. Standards (mandatory): - "Traffic control devices or their supports shall not bear any advertising message or any other message that is not related to traffic control." - "CMS shall display only traffic operational, regulatory, warning, and guidance information except as otherwise provided in this Chapter. Advertising or other messages not related to traffic control shall not be displayed on a CMS or on its supports or other equipment." - "Traffic control devices, public announcements or notices, and other signs or messages within the highway right-of-way shall be placed only as authorized by a public authority or the official having jurisdiction... for the purpose of regulating, warning, or guiding traffic." Support (informational): - States are encouraged to adopt, through policy or legislation, the provisions of 23 CFR 750.108 that restrict outdoor advertising from resembling traffic control devices. - Traffic control devices are defined as devices whose primary purpose is communicating a regulatory, warning, or guidance message to road users. Citations: - Section 1D.07 Standard §1 (p.34) - Section 2L.02 Standard §1 (p.511) - Section 1D.02 Standard §3 (p.31) - Section 1D.02 Support §6 (p.32) - Section 6A.03 Standard §2 (p.768) - Section 1A.02 Support §1 (p.1)
gold_answer: No. They may not bear advertising or any message unrelated to traffic control. Acknowledgment signs, Specific Service signs, and Tourist-Oriented Directional signs are not treated as advertising under this provision.
